strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the limitations of hand-engineered tool APIs in SWE agents with timely focus on computer-use paradigms

Comprehensive and well-designed environment supporting multiple languages (8), modalities (text/image/video/audio), and rich IDE tools with proper infrastructure (Docker, checkpointing, gymnasium API)

Extensive benchmark with 5400 instances across 15 diverse tasks from 13 existing datasets plus 2 novel contributions, with principled curation across task types and a lightweight variant for accessibility

Thorough and honest experimental analysis evaluating multiple VLMs with systematic failure mode analysis, clear documentation of limitations, and valuable insights from 'assisted' experiments showing up to 13.3% improvement with proper tools
Clear identification and documentation of current model limitations including visual grounding failures, file editing difficulties, and insufficient IDE tool usage with concrete examples
Solid technical execution with proper infrastructure design, detailed implementation descriptions, comprehensive appendices, and promised reproducibility resources
weaknesses: Core thesis significantly undermined by results showing computer-use agents achieve only 10.2% vs 46.8% with API tools—a 4.6× gap suggesting the approach fundamentally struggles without structured tool interfaces, which validates rather than challenges the tool-based paradigm
Evaluation limited to 300 of 5400 instances (PwP-Bench-Lite) due to computational constraints, limiting confidence in result generalization and reducing the benchmark's practical impact

Unfair comparisons with prior work using different trajectory lengths (55% on SWE-Bench achieved with longer trajectories vs PwP's 20-step limit), model versions, and computational budgets, though acknowledged, still presented prominently

Limited technical novelty—primarily combines existing components (computer-use agents, unified benchmarks) into an SWE-specific environment without fundamental algorithmic or methodological innovations

Critical unresolved problems: visual grounding issues remain fundamentally unsolved beyond Set-of-Marks (existing technique); no novel solutions proposed despite this being identified as the primary bottleneck

Insufficient root cause analysis of why computer-use dramatically underperforms—unclear whether the limitation is the paradigm itself, implementation details, or model training, making it hard to assess future viability

Design choices lack justification: 20-step trajectory limit appears arbitrary and could disadvantage computer-use approaches; no sensitivity analysis provided; task selection criteria could be more explicit

Evaluation metric concerns: macro-averaging across heterogeneous metrics from different datasets (accuracy, F1, pass@k operating at different scales) may not be meaningful; should report task-specific results more prominently

Missing critical comparisons: no evaluation of how existing tool-based agents perform when adapted to PwP, preventing assessment of whether tool-based paradigm is inherently superior or better suited to training

Incomplete trade-off analysis: paper doesn't thoroughly discuss how tool-based approaches provide structure/interpretability/efficiency while computer-use trades these for generality, or clarify when each paradigm is preferable
Generalization concerns: VSCode-specific design limits transferability to other IDEs; IDE-specific shortcuts may reduce long-term value as tools evolve
Code/data release link missing ('We release code and data at [blank]'), affecting reproducibility claims despite other documentation efforts

strengths: Well-motivated contribution establishing software engineering as an important domain for evaluating computer-use agents

Comprehensive, well-engineered environment (PwP) with expressive action/observation spaces, full IDE tooling access, multimodal support across 14 languages, and reproducible Docker-based infrastructure
Substantial benchmark (PwP-Bench) unifying 15 diverse SWE tasks from 13 existing datasets plus 2 new ones, spanning multiple task categories and modalities
Thorough empirical evaluation with multiple agent designs, 9 model variants, and detailed failure mode analysis identifying concrete limitations (visual grounding, tool usage)
Clear quantitative findings showing dramatic performance gap (22.9% visual → 50.7% with APIs) and actionable insights for future work
Strong infrastructure design with state checkpointing, gymnasium interface, and commitment to open-source release enabling future research
Detailed qualitative analysis with concrete failure examples, including assisted experiments showing 13.3% potential gains from better tool use
weaknesses: Main evaluation limited to PwP-Bench-Lite (300 instances, 5.5% of 5,400 full benchmark) due to computational constraints, raising generalizability concerns and making claims about the full benchmark speculative

Significant step budget limitations (20 steps for main experiments) with only limited 250-step results for 1 model on 3 datasets; unclear how much performance is artificially suppressed for longer-horizon SWE-Bench tasks

Weak specialized baseline: mini-sweagent (48.8%) used in main paper while SOTA ranges 74-75%, making headline claims that CUAs 'approach specialized agents' misleading; SOTA comparison relegated to appendix
Set-of-Marks (SoM) DOM augmentations presented as standard but represent significant assistance; unclear performance degradation without SoM, and their necessity contradicts 'pure visual' positioning
File/Bash API comparisons claim operations are 'theoretically' performable visually, yet the 2.2x performance gap (22.9% vs 50.7%) suggests fundamental differences that aren't fully analyzed
Minimal statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing on most results except one McNemar's test; visual grounding error analysis based on only 20 manual trajectories
Metric aggregation using 'macro averages' across orthogonal metrics from different datasets obscures patterns; datasets with vastly different difficulties weighted equally
Limited methodological novelty: environment + benchmark + evaluation work without novel agent architectures, training methods, or algorithmic contributions limits impact for methods-focused venues
